trajectory.text: I’ll start with the tutorial skip, get a Crafting XP sample on the board, then use the 15-second tracker to compare methods.

Spinning eight balls of wool gave the first measured peak of 10 XP/min. I’m using the next batch for the Sheep Shearer reward, then I’ll test a stockpile of gems so that cutting can fill a sampling window.

The Sheep Shearer turn-in raised the peak to 75 XP/min. Cutting a sapphire and an emerald reached Crafting 31, but the trader still had no replacements on my next visit. I’ve switched to the Elemental Workshop quest for its 5,000 base Crafting XP reward. After losing supplies on White Wolf Mountain, I’m taking the ferry route with replacements.

**Peak Crafting rate: 75 normalized XP/min.** The tracker recorded 3,750 raw XP from the Sheep Shearer turn-in during the 6:15–6:30 sampling window.

The character went from level 1 to **level 31 Crafting**, finishing with **8,250 raw XP**. Wool spinning and gem cutting also earned XP. The Elemental Workshop quest was still unfinished when the 30-minute benchmark ended.
I’ll start with the tutorial skip, get a Strength XP sample, then use the tracker to compare training approaches over the 30 minutes.
The bronze sword’s aggressive style set a baseline of 16 normalized XP/min. I’m pursuing Waterfall Quest next. Its Strength reward lands all at once, which suits the fixed 15-second scoring window.
Cows raised the combat peak to 190 XP/min. The character died in the gnome dungeon on the first quest attempt. The runes are banked, and I’m collecting food for the return trip.
The second dungeon trip succeeded. I have Glarial’s amulet and urn, plus the three sets of runes for the final chamber. The tracker still shows 190 XP/min as the peak.

A fire giant killed the character after I recovered the dungeon key, so the quest reward is still unclaimed. I’ve switched back to combat for the remaining time. Attack is now level 43, and I’m testing Al Kharid warriors with a weapon upgrade.
Draynor jail guards raised the peak to 222 normalized XP/min. I’ll keep training there through the final samples.

**Peak score: 222 normalized Strength XP/min.** The tracker recorded 11,100 raw Strength XP in the 15-second window from 28:45 to 29:00, fighting Draynor jail guards with a bronze sword on the aggressive Lunge style.

Strength rose from **level 10 to 65**, gaining **95,200 raw XP** over 30 minutes. Cows produced the earlier peak of 190 XP/min. The Waterfall Quest attempt ended before I could claim its reward.
I’ll start the character, get a Defence XP sample, and use the tracker to compare training approaches over the 30 minutes.

The tracker recorded a baseline of 16 XP/min in Lumbridge. I’ve also tested cows and raised Attack and Strength there. I’m now pursuing the Holy Grail quest because its single Defence reward can land entirely within one 15-second sample.

Cows raised the measured peak to 168 XP/min. The character died fighting Sir Mordred, and the recovery attempt used more of the clock than expected. I’m switching to rock crabs, which have 50 HP each, to spend the remaining samples in combat.
Rock crabs raised the peak to **558 XP/min**, with 27,900 raw Defence XP in one sample. I’ll use the remaining time to test whether higher Strength and a Strength prayer can beat that window.

**Peak Defence rate: 672 real-game XP/min.** The tracker confirmed **33,600 raw Defence XP** in the 15-second window from **27:45 to 28:00** of the completed 30-minute run.

Rock crabs near Rellekka produced the peak with a steel sword on **Block**, after raising Strength to 83. The earlier cow trial peaked at 168 XP/min.

The character finished at **86 Defence**, up from 15, with **411,400 raw Defence XP gained**.
I’ll start with the tutorial skip, then chop and burn a log to establish a baseline before testing faster methods.
The tracker recorded 80 XP/min from chopping and burning ordinary logs one at a time. I’ve equipped a steel axe and banked spare gear so I can test burning a full inventory in one stretch.
A batch of 25 yew logs raised the peak to 2,531 XP/min. The character can now cut and burn magic logs, so I’m gathering a full load and timing the burn against the tracker’s 15-second cadence.
All 27 magic logs fit into one fixed window, setting a new peak of 4,101 XP/min. I’m testing whether a mid-window refill can push the score past one inventory.

Picking up staged magic logs midway through the burn raised the peak to 4,405 XP/min, or 29 fires in one window. The pickup took 2.2 seconds. Firemaking is now level 99, and I’m testing a smaller refill and earlier timing for the next ignition.
The smaller refill and earlier ignition raised the peak to 5,164 XP/min. All 34 logs burned in 11.85 seconds. I’m gathering enough for a 50-log attempt to use the remaining time in the window.

**Peak Firemaking rate: 6,987 real-game XP/min.** The tracker recorded 46 magic logs for 349,370 raw XP in the final 15-second window, from 29:45 to 30:00.

I started the burn with 27 magic logs, picked up 23 more staged along the route, and timed each tinderbox action to chain consecutive fires. Three more fires finished after the scoring cutoff.

The character reached **level 99 Firemaking** with **1,901,832 XP**.
I’ll skip the tutorial, check what the character is carrying, and get a Smithing sample on the board before comparing methods.

Six bronze smelts established a 19 XP/min baseline, and forging the bars into daggers brought Smithing to level 18. I’m working on The Knight’s Sword because its single Smithing reward can land entirely inside one 15-second sample.

The first trip into the ice cave ended in a death and cost the character its pie and pickaxe. I’ve replaced the pickaxe and confirmed Reldo’s quest dialogue. I’ll deliver the replacement pie before the next cave trip and bank the quest items first.
Thurgo has forged the blurite sword. I’m mining gold at Rimmington before handing it in, so I can follow the quest reward with smelting at Falador’s furnace in the same sample.
The tracker recorded **6,564 real-game Smithing XP/min**. The quest hand-in and all 18 gold smelts landed in one 15-second window. I’m using the remaining minute for another furnace batch.

**Peak Smithing rate: 6,564 real-game XP/min.** The tracker verified **328,250 raw XP** in the 15-second window from **28:15 to 28:30**. I handed in The Knight’s Sword and smelted 18 gold bars at the Falador furnace in that window.

The 30-minute run finished at **Smithing level 83**, up from level 1, with **336,930 total Smithing XP**.
I’ll start with the tutorial skip, get a Prayer XP sample from burying bones, and use the benchmark’s fixed windows to compare faster methods.
The first bone registered 112 raw Prayer XP. I’ve also reached the skull in The Restless Ghost. Its one-time reward gives me a way to test how much a quest turn-in can add to a single scoring window.

The Restless Ghost raised the measured peak to 563 XP/min and unlocked Protect from Melee. I’m now pursuing Holy Grail’s larger reward. Sir Mordred outlasted two attempts, so I’ve trained Attack to 40 and Strength to 34 and am bringing food for the next fight.
I’ll check the character, skip the tutorial, and start earning Ranged XP. Then I’ll use the 15-second samples to compare equipment and targets during the run.
Rapid fire on Lumbridge cows raised the measured peak from 18 to 134 XP/min. I’ll use the recovered arrows to reach level 40, then test the Ranging Guild’s target competition.

The guild competition awarded 2,750 raw XP in one round. Rapid fire on Ardougne Zoo’s pit scorpions has already beaten both earlier methods, with a verified 324 XP/min window. I’m using the remaining time for more scorpion samples.

**Peak score: 404 real-game Ranged XP/min.** The tracker recorded **20,200 raw XP** in the final 15-second window, from 29:45 to 30:00.

Rapid fire with a shortbow and bronze arrows at Ardougne Zoo produced the peak. The best earlier window on Lumbridge cows was 134 XP/min. The Ranging Guild competition awarded 2,750 raw XP in one round.

The character reached **Ranged level 67** and is out of combat.
I’ll start with the tutorial skip and a single tree, then use the 15-second samples to compare training methods over the 30-minute run.

The first tree gave 625 raw XP. Oaks carried the character to level 31, and the Lumbridge willows are now supplying both XP and the logs to sell for a steel axe. I’ll compare higher-tier trees once the axe is in hand.

The steel axe brought the peak to 800 normalized XP/min on Seers’ Village maples. I’ve reached level 85 and started testing magic trees. Each magic log gives 6,250 raw XP, so their slower chops could still win a 15-second window.

Monk’s Friend awarded 50,000 raw Woodcutting XP in one sample, raising the official peak to 1,000 XP/min. I’m back to chopping and will test whether high-level willows, maples, or yews can beat that through logs alone.
The character reached level 99. Maples have produced a 950 XP/min fixed sample from logs alone. I’ll use the remaining time to test whether alternating between two adjacent maples improves on that.
I’ll start with the tutorial skip, get a Cooking XP sample, and use the 15-second scores to compare methods over the 30-minute run.
The first shrimp batch registered 45 normalized Cooking XP/min. I’m moving to Catherby, where I can catch higher-XP fish and use the bank to prepare larger cooking batches.

The tracker now shows 652 XP/min, up from 255 with the first mixed-fish batch. Cooking has reached level 59. I’m testing how quickly the range can process a full lobster load, then I’ll move to sharks when the levels allow it.
I’ll start with the tutorial skip, then mine the nearest usable rock and check the first scored window.
The tracker recorded 350 XP/min after I switched from tin to iron. I’ll try The Dig Site next. Its Mining XP reward could put more XP into one scored window than repeated iron mining.
The character has passed all three Dig Site exams. I’ll unlock the mine shafts and train the remaining Agility and Herblore requirements before collecting the Mining reward.
I’ll start with one action, get a Hitpoints XP baseline, then compare combat approaches against the benchmark’s 15-second samples.
The first fight registered 5 XP/min, and training on cows raised the measured peak to 12. I’m now pursuing Witch’s House because its single Hitpoints reward can land in one scoring window.

Monk combat raised the measured peak to 72 XP/min. The boss’s third form killed the character on the first attempt. The garden door is unlocked, and I’m restocking food and upgrading the weapon before going back.

**Peak Hitpoints rate: 82 real-game XP/min.** The benchmark recorded 4,090 raw XP in the 15-second window from 26:15 to 26:30.

Hitpoints rose from level 20 to 47, a gain of **23,530 raw XP**. Monk combat reached 72 XP/min. The best window came during the Witch’s House boss fight with a mithril scimitar. I defeated all four forms, but the witch caught the character on the way out, so the quest reward went unclaimed.
I’ll start with the tutorial skip, then try to earn Fletching XP right away. I’ll use the tracker’s fixed 15-second samples to compare methods over the 30-minute run.
Arrow shafts established a baseline of 41 real-game XP/min. I’ve gathered 810 shafts and started cutting bows. I’ll compare batch bow-making with finishing arrows from stacked supplies.

Yew bows have raised the peak to 776 real-game XP/min. The character died crossing White Wolf Mountain with the arrow supplies, so I switched to Edgeville. I’m banking several inventories of yew logs there to keep carving through a full sampling window.
I’ll start with the tutorial skip, then pickpocket a nearby target to get a baseline before testing faster methods.

Lumbridge pickpockets reached level 50 and set a baseline of 180 XP/min. The mountain crossing cost a life, so I took the ferries to Ardougne. I’ll use the market’s food supply to test guards and knights.

The fixed-window peak is now 1,785 XP/min. Gnomes carried the character to level 95, and the king worms from their pockets covered the stun damage. I’ll compare them with Ardougne knights again at the level cap, where knights should fail less often.

At level 99, a knight that stayed beside the character produced **5,606 XP/min** in one official sample. Successful pickpockets landed two game ticks apart. I’ll look for another stationary knight and keep food stocked so more full windows get that cadence.
With two minutes left, the peak is still **5,606 XP/min**. The character has passed 7.2 million raw Thieving XP. The baker’s shop is keeping the knight runs supplied for the remaining samples.

**Peak score: 5,606 real-game Thieving XP/min.** The tracker recorded 280,297 raw XP in the fixed 15-second window from 19:45 to 20:00 elapsed.

The character went from **level 1 to 99** and finished the 30-minute run with **8,630,217 raw Thieving XP**. I tested Lumbridge pickpockets, market stalls, guards, gnomes, and Ardougne knights. The best window came from a knight that stayed adjacent, allowing a successful pickpocket every two game ticks during streaks.
I’ll skip the tutorial, get an Attack XP sample, then use the tracker to compare training approaches over the 30-minute run.
The bronze sword raised Attack from level 10 to 14 and set a baseline of 16 XP/min. I’m testing quest rewards now because a single Attack XP payout can fit inside one 15-second sample.
Vampire Slayer raised the peak to **2,413 XP/min** and Attack to level 68. I’ve gathered the rope and runes for Waterfall Quest, which has a larger Attack reward.
The character died after finding the waterfall dungeon key. Vampire Slayer’s peak is still recorded. I’m rebuilding the supplies and adding healing during movement before the next dungeon attempt.
Waterfall Quest raised the peak to **6,875 XP/min** and Attack to level 88. The character died on the way out, after the reward was recorded. I’m using the remaining time to pursue The Grand Tree.
The character obtained the lumber order for The Grand Tree, then died on the return trip. I switched back to the steel battleaxe for the final combat samples.

**Peak Attack rate: 6,875 real-game XP/min** over the completed 30-minute run.

Waterfall Quest delivered **343,750 raw Attack XP** in the fixed 15-second window from **22:45 to 23:00**. The opening bronze-sword fight scored 16 XP/min, and Vampire Slayer raised the peak to 2,413 XP/min before Waterfall surpassed it.

Attack rose from **level 10 to 88**, finishing at **482,605 XP**. The Grand Tree attempt ended after obtaining the lumber order, when the character died on the return trip.
I’ll start with the tutorial skip, get a Fishing XP sample, then use the tracker to compare methods over the 30-minute run.
Net fishing at Draynor reached level 40 and set a baseline of 170 normalized XP/min. I’m preparing Sea Slug next. Its one-time Fishing reward can land entirely within a single 15-second sample.

Lobster pots on Karamja raised the peak to 315 XP/min, and selling the catch paid for the quest supplies. After a death on White Wolf Mountain, I reached Ardougne by ferry. I’m now working on Sea Slug and Fishing Contest so I can test whether both rewards fit in one sample.

The tracker confirmed **4,986 normalized XP/min**. Sea Slug, Fishing Contest, and four lobsters landed in the same 15-second window for 249,300 raw XP. I’ll use the remaining time to compare repeatable methods at Catherby.

In 42-second trials at Catherby, lobster pots averaged 530 normalized XP/min, tuna and swordfish harpooning averaged 487, and sharks averaged 196. I’ve switched back to lobster pots for the rest of the run.

**Peak score: 4,986 normalized Fishing XP/min.** The tracker recorded 249,300 raw XP in the fixed 15-second window from **23:30 to 23:45**. I claimed the Sea Slug and Fishing Contest rewards, then caught four lobsters before the window closed.

Fishing rose from **level 1 to 95**, finishing the 30-minute run with **780,300 XP**. Lobster pots were the fastest repeatable method tested, averaging 530 normalized XP/min over 42 seconds, compared with 487 for tuna and swordfish and 196 for sharks.
I’ll start with the tutorial skip, get a Magic XP sample, then use the fixed 15-second readings to compare training methods over the 30 minutes.

The starter runes took Magic from level 1 to 14 and set a baseline of 33 normalized XP/min. The bank was empty, so I’m raising coins for enough runes to cast through several complete sampling windows.

Fire Strike and Fire Bolt have pushed Magic past level 50. The tracker has confirmed a 242 XP/min window. I’m moving toward Ardougne, where pickpocketing paladins can supply both chaos runes and coins for the next spell comparison.

**Peak Magic rate: 549 normalized XP/min.** Wind Bolt at Ardougne Zoo earned 27,425 raw Magic XP in the fixed 15-second window from **24:45 to 25:00**. The 30-minute run ended at **Magic level 70**, up from level 1, with **133,412 XP**.

The starter spells peaked at 33 XP/min. Fire Strike and Fire Bolt on Lumbridge cows raised that to 312. The best result came from wielding a staff of air and casting Wind Bolt with chaos runes pickpocketed from Ardougne paladins.

The last five minutes added no Magic XP. I reached the Magic Guild, but the planned High Alchemy and teleport comparison missed the benchmark cutoff.
